analysis.investment_thesis: A sub-INR 156 Cr micro-cap consulting outfit earning a pathetic 0.41% ROE fails every Munger quality test — the business is producing returns far below the cost of capital. Inverting the question "what could go wrong?" yields an easy answer: almost everything already has.
key_strengths: Low reported P/E of 12.4x (but on near-zero earnings, which is meaningless)
Promoter holding of 43.9% indicates some skin in the game
Asset-light consulting model in principle requires minimal capex
key_risks: ROE of 0.41% — business earns essentially nothing on equity, far below bond yields
Negligible institutional interest (FII 0.19%, DII 0.01%) signals no serious scrutiny
Tiny INR 156 Cr cap + undifferentiated 'consulting/auditing/market research' offers no moat
red_flags: ROE of 0.41% is an order of magnitude below my 15% threshold
Vague, kitchen-sink business description (legal + accounting + polling + consultancy) — a classic di-worsification red flag
Promoter holds under 50% — no clear controlling discipline, with 56% floating in retail hands
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Inverting, as I always do: what would make this a disaster? A business with 0.41% return on equity IS the disaster — capital deployed here is destroying value in real terms once you account for inflation and opportunity cost. The P/E of 12.4 is a statistical illusion; on a near-zero earnings base, small absolute swings produce wild multiples. The laundry-list business description — legal, accounting, auditing, tax, market research, opinion polling, management consultancy — violates the Munger principle of understanding a durable franchise. This is not a business; it is a corporate shell doing whatever pays the bills this quarter.

Negligible institutional ownership (0.20% combined FII+DII) tells you the professionals who scrutinize businesses for a living have taken one look and walked away. There is no moat, no scale, no brand, no network effect, no switching cost — just a tiny services firm competing against the Big Four at the top and thousands of CA practices at the bottom. Munger's rule: the first filter is whether a business meets quality standards; only then do you discuss price. This one doesn't clear the first filter. Pass, and find something you can actually understand and admire.
